close_reason:
Applied both recommended defences across all 8 extension-client crates' SessionClient impls:

(a) Compile-time assertion '_assert_session_client_send_sync()' (top-level, #[allow(dead_code)]) in each crate's methods/mod.rs that calls assert_send_sync::<SessionClient>(). The static body 'fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}' panics at compile time if a future jmap-base-client release adds a !Sync interior-mutability field to JmapClient or Session — turning a downstream caller's cryptic 'cannot send between threads safely' error into a dependency-upgrade-time compile error at the kit boundary.

(b) Doc-comment '# Thread safety' section on every SessionClient struct stating that SessionClient is Send + Sync, that the type can be shared via Arc<SessionClient> or cloned for per-task ownership, and that a Send/Sync regression in jmap-base-client would be major-version-breaking for this crate. Each section cross-references the compile-time assertion as the regression guard.

Workspace canonical-template propagation: changed mail-client first, then propagated cookie-cutter to chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing/metadata. All 8 SessionClient impls now carry both the doc and the assertion. No behavior change; rustdoc clean across the workspace.
description:
mod.rs:362-364 (doc comment on SessionClient):

  "Clone is derived because JmapClient is itself cheap-to-clone (it
   already implements Clone and with_mail_session clones one internally),
   enabling parallel-task fan-out with one bound session."

"Parallel-task fan-out" implies Send + Sync, but the type does not document its auto-trait contract explicitly. Today SessionClient is Send + Sync transitively because:

  - jmap_base_client::JmapClient is Send + Sync (uses reqwest::Client internally)
  - jmap_base_client::Session is Send + Sync (plain Serde-derived data)

But neither is GUARANTEED by jmap_base_client's docs to remain Send + Sync. A future jmap_base_client refactor that adds a !Sync interior-mutability field to JmapClient (e.g. a Cell<...> for request-id counter) would silently break SessionClient's auto-trait inheritance, and downstream callers would get cryptic "cannot send between threads safely" errors with no migration story.

This is the classic auto-trait-leakage problem. Two contract-defence options:

  (a) Add a compile-time assertion in tests/ that statically requires Send + Sync:

      #[test]
      fn session_client_is_send_sync() {
          fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
          assert_send_sync::<SessionClient>();
      }

      This catches accidental regressions in a future jmap_base_client bump.

  (b) Document explicitly in the rustdoc that SessionClient is Send + Sync and that this is a stability commitment:

      "# Thread safety
       SessionClient is Send + Sync. The inner JmapClient and Session are
       both Send + Sync per jmap_base_client's contract, so this type can
       be shared across async tasks. If a future jmap_base_client release
       drops Send or Sync on either, that is a major-version-breaking
       change for this crate."

Recommendation: BOTH. Test + doc. Same applies across six sibling extension-client crates.

Cross-reference: JMAP-tjvm.17 (re-export major-version coupling) raises the same family of risk: auto-trait inheritance is just as fragile as concrete-type re-exports.

Priority P3 — today the code works; the risk is future-regression. Cheap to defend with the compile-time assertion.

Mark says NO HUMAN — Recommendation: add the static assertion test and the Thread safety docstring section.
title: SessionClient: Send + Sync concurrency contract not documented despite Clone-for-parallel-fan-out doc-comment promise
